newsitem.title: LEBANON: Six civilians said killed in S. Lebanon shelling.
newsitem.headline: Six civilians said killed in S. Lebanon shelling.

text.p: A militia led by a pro-Israeli commander fired shells at the southern port city of Sidon on Monday, killing six civilians and wounding 34, many of them seriously.
The Israeli army said forces under the command of pro-Israeli militia leader Antoine Lahd were behind the attack.

Lahd is commander of the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) in an Israeli-held occupation zone and of a militia force in the Jezzine area just outside the zone. The army said this second group was responsible.
"The SLA is backed by Israel whereas the people who fired are not backed by Israel," an Israeli military source insisted.
Military sources said the shelling followed an increase in attacks on the Jezzine area.
The army said two Lebanese youths were killed and two wounded hours earlier when an explosive device blew up a vehicle in the Jezzine area.
A total of 16 shells landed in Sidon and its suburbs, forcing residents to abandon the city's main road and many shops to close.
Security sources in Lebanon put the death toll at six and said 34 were hurt in the attack on Sidon, located 40 km (25 miles) south of Beirut.
Victims were rushed to five hospitals where doctors tried to identify the dead.

"We have two heads and parts of bodies in the post-mortem room. Many people came but nobody was able to identify them. We still don't know who they belong to," said a medic at Sidon's Ghassan Hamoud hospital.
The wounded tried to make sense of the violence.

"I heard an explosion close to my door and went out to check. I suddenly found myself sinking in blood and now I am here. That's all I know," said Ibrahim Shabaan, 70, half of his head covered by a bandage.
Ten-year-old Wissam was playing soccer with his friends when a shell struck nearby.
"I was playing with my friends with a ball. A bomb hit the barber shop. It left a hole in my leg," he told Reuters.

Shortly after the shelling subsided, six Katyusha rockets struck Jezzine, an SLA stronghold just north of Israel's south Lebanon security zone, where Israeli forces and Hizbollah guerrillas often engage in fierce clashes.
Hizbollah sources in Beirut said they had no immediate information on the rocket attacks.
Hizbollah's top official in south Lebanon, Nabeel Kawouk, threatened to carry out reprisals for the shelling by pro-Israeli militias.

"We must speak in the language that the Israeli enemy understands and it is not possible to keep silent about what happened today. The enemy must understand a deeply bitter message," he told reporters after visiting some of the wounded in Sidon hospitals.
